verdict.rationale: Snowflake documents bulk operations at several levels. Data can be bulk-copied into and out of tables with COPY INTO, and a hands-on user confirms it loads arbitrarily many files and skips ones already loaded. Snowpipe loads files in micro-batches. Container-level actions apply to many objects at once: Time Travel can restore all objects inside a database or schema, and cloning carries privileges across all child objects. Those set-based SQL statements can be submitted programmatically through the SQL API. missing for 10: explicit documentation of batch/bulk endpoints in the resource-management REST API, agent-oriented guidance (e.g., via MCP or CLI) for bulk actions across many objects, broader independent corroboration beyond one community tip.
